information.description:
These are by and large the best fighters the Animals have to offer. They’re fast, hard to kill, and likely have a championship win under their belt — often literally (they like to brag). Thickskulls adhere to Animal philosophy harder than most, and as such dissuade from all firearms in favor of just crushing skulls with their bare hands.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Animals).

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.
Throwing hands, does not ignore half armor.

Cost Per Dose: 1,000eb (Very Expensive)

The Animals' favorite drink, a miracle elixir, the dream-come-true of every scrawny, twig-limbed skeleton that dreams of having boulders and chesticles. Warning, may result in: priapism (perpetual painful erection), gynecomastia (enlarged breasts), balding, hair growth, acne, kidney failure, muscle tearing, prostate cancer, jaundice, pruritic rashes, liver fibrosis, liver cancer, or liver failure.

⋙ PRIMARY EFFECT ⋘

  • Lasts for 1 Month.
  • The User takes 1d6 Humanity loss upon taking a dose.
  • Juice cannot be administered during combat, and requires a full 24 hours spent doing nothing else to administer. Multiple doses of Juice within the same Month provide no additional benefit and will cause the user to overdose, requiring immediate hospitalization and Addiction Therapy (CP:R, pg. 230).
  • While under the Primary Effect of Juice, the User’s BODY is increased by 3. This affects the user’s HP and Death Saves, and stacks with any of the user’s Cyberware or other effects.
  • User experiences more animalistic urges that cause outbursts of rage. Do your best to roleplay accordingly.
  • This drug has no effect on FBCs or users with Internal Linear Frames, due to a lack of enough organic muscle left to enhance.

⋙ SECONDARY EFFECT (DV29) ⋘

  • If the user wasn’t addicted to Juice, they are now. While addicted, the user’s COOL is permanently decreased by 2 and their REF is permanently decreased by 1 (Minimum 1).
  • While addicted and not experiencing the Primary Effect of Juice, the User craves more Juice and their BODY and MOVE are decreased by 2 (Minimum 1).
  • Rapidetox ends the Primary Effects of Juice but has no effect otherwise. The user is Addicted until they undergo Addiction Therapy.

NOTE: Credit to the From the Ashes LC for the original version of this item.

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive) per dose
Type: Street Drug

Foundry notes:

  • While addicted, switch on the "Juice Addiction" effect.
  • When an addicted character doses, use "Juice Addicted Primary" instead of the normal primary effect; it cancels the withdrawal penalties for the duration.
  • Stat and skill changes are automated; caps, minimums, durations, and everything else are not.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Gear, Drugs, & Frames > Consumables > Street Drugs).

Primary Effect

Dose lasts 24 hours.

  • The user rolls 2d6 Humanity Loss which is returned if they pass the Secondary Effect save
  • The user ignores Seriously Wounded wound states for the duration

Secondary Effect (DV17)

When the dose wears off, the user rolls WILL + Resist Torture/Drugs + 1d10 against Secondary DV.

  • On Fail Humanity loss is not returned
  • Unless experiencing the primary effect, REF -2

Run the edge at top speed, choomba. There ain’t another way to live.

Speedware. As an Action, the user may activate this cyberware, after which it remains active for the next 60 seconds (20 Rounds). While active, this cyberware provides a +3 bonus to any Initiative Roll made. If activated while the user is already in an Initiative Queue, their current Initiative increases by 3, which is lost if this cyberware deactivates or its duration expires during combat. This cyberware has a 1 hour cooldown before it can be activated again. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Clinic
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Sandevistan; use this one instead of the core item.
  • Matches the core item's setup: the +3 shows as a toggle in the initiative roll dialog.
